questions.question: Two tuning forks vibrate at $f_1 = 440\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and $f_2 = 444\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Find the beat frequency.
questions.answer:
$f_{\text{beat}} = |f_1 - f_2| = |440 - 444| = 4\ \mathrm{Hz}$

The loudness of the combined sound pulses 4 times per second.

questions.question: Derive the beat frequency formula $f_{\text{beat}} = |f_1 - f_2|$ by adding two cosine waves of slightly different frequencies.
questions.answer:
$y = \cos(2\pi f_1 t) + \cos(2\pi f_2 t)$

Using sum-to-product:

$y = 2\cos\left(\pi(f_1-f_2)t\right)\cos\left(\pi(f_1+f_2)t\right)$

Let $\bar{f} = (f_1+f_2)/2$ (average frequency, audible tone) and $\delta f = (f_1-f_2)/2$:

$y = 2\cos(2\pi \delta f\, t) \cdot \cos(2\pi\bar{f}\, t)$

The amplitude $2\cos(2\pi\delta f\, t)$ oscillates at frequency $|\delta f| = |f_1-f_2|/2$.

The **intensity** (proportional to amplitude squared) peaks twice per cycle of the amplitude envelope: beat frequency $= 2 \times |\delta f| = |f_1 - f_2|$.

questions.question: A standard tuning fork ($A = 440\ \mathrm{Hz}$) and an unknown fork produce 6 beats/s. The unknown fork is tightened (increasing its frequency) and the beats decrease to 2/s. Find the original and final frequencies of the unknown fork.
questions.answer:
Unknown fork produces 6 beats with 440 Hz: $f_u = 440 \pm 6$, so either $446$ or $434\ \mathrm{Hz}$.

After tightening (increasing $f_u$), beats decrease to 2/s. If $f_u$ increases and beats decrease, then $f_u$ was moving **closer** to 440:

- If $f_u = 434$: increasing gives $f_u \to 436$, beats $= |436-440| = 4$ (not 2)
- If $f_u = 434$: to get 2 beats, $f_u$ must reach $442$
- Actually: if $f_u$ was $446$ (above 440), increasing would give more beats, not fewer.

$f_u$ was $434\ \mathrm{Hz}$ originally. After tightening: $f_u = 438\ \mathrm{Hz}$ (gives 2 beats with 440) ✓

But wait: $434 \to 438$ means 4 Hz increase. Or: $f_u$ was $434$, after tightening $f_u = 438$ giving $|438-440|=2$ ✓.

**Answer:** Original $f_u = 434\ \mathrm{Hz}$; after tightening, $f_u = 438\ \mathrm{Hz}$.

questions.question: A guitar string is tuned to $f_0 = 330\ \mathrm{Hz}$. When played with a $335\ \mathrm{Hz}$ reference tone, 5 beats/s are heard. The string is loosened slightly (decreasing tension). The beats become faster. Is the string frequency above or below $335\ \mathrm{Hz}$?
questions.answer:
5 beats/s means the string is at $330\ \mathrm{Hz}$ or $340\ \mathrm{Hz}$.

Wait — the string was tuned to 330 Hz originally, but the question says 5 beats with 335 Hz reference, so string is at $335 \pm 5 = 330$ or $340$ Hz.

If string is at **330 Hz** and we **loosen** (decrease frequency, say to 328 Hz): beats = $|328 - 335| = 7$ → more beats ✓

If string is at **340 Hz** and we **loosen** (decrease to 338 Hz): beats = $|338 - 335| = 3$ → fewer beats ✗

**The string frequency is below $335\ \mathrm{Hz}$** (at $330\ \mathrm{Hz}$). Loosening moves it further from 335 Hz, increasing beat frequency.

questions.question: Two sources emit sounds of $f_1 = 512\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and $f_2 = 508\ \mathrm{Hz}$. Find: (a) the beat frequency, (b) the period of the beats, (c) the average audible frequency.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $f_{\text{beat}} = |512 - 508| = 4\ \mathrm{Hz}$

**(b)** $T_{\text{beat}} = 1/f_{\text{beat}} = 1/4 = 0.25\ \mathrm{s}$

**(c)** Average frequency: $\bar{f} = (512 + 508)/2 = 510\ \mathrm{Hz}$ — this is the pitch you hear fluctuating at 4 Hz.

questions.question: Two strings on a musical instrument have frequencies $f_1 = 396\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and $f_2 = 400\ \mathrm{Hz}$. They are plucked simultaneously at $t = 0$. At what times $t > 0$ do the two waves first constructively interfere (maximum beat)?
questions.answer:
Beat period: $T_{\text{beat}} = 1/f_{\text{beat}} = 1/|f_1-f_2| = 1/4 = 0.25\ \mathrm{s}$

At $t = 0$, both waves start in phase (maximum constructive interference).

The next maximum (beat peak) occurs one full beat cycle later:

$t = T_{\text{beat}} = 0.25\ \mathrm{s}$, $0.50\ \mathrm{s}$, $0.75\ \mathrm{s}$, $\ldots$

Minimum (destructive interference, silence) occurs at:

$t = T_{\text{beat}}/2 = 0.125\ \mathrm{s}$, $0.375\ \mathrm{s}$, $\ldots$

questions.question: A piano technician is tuning a string to middle C ($f_0 = 261.6\ \mathrm{Hz}$). She hears 3 beats/s. After slightly tightening the string, she hears 4 beats/s. Was the string originally too high or too low in frequency?
questions.answer:
3 beats/s: string is at $261.6 \pm 3\ \mathrm{Hz}$, so $258.6$ or $264.6\ \mathrm{Hz}$.

After tightening (increasing frequency): 4 beats/s.

If string was at **264.6** (above): increasing gives, say, 266 Hz, beats = $|266-261.6| = 4.4 \approx 4$ ✓ (moving further away)

If string was at **258.6** (below): increasing gives, say, 260.6 Hz, beats = $|260.6-261.6| = 1$ — fewer beats, not 4. ✗

**The string was too high** ($264.6\ \mathrm{Hz}$). Tightening moved it further from $261.6\ \mathrm{Hz}$, increasing beats.

questions.question: Two speakers emit at $f_1 = 1000\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and $f_2 = 1003\ \mathrm{Hz}$. How many times per second does a listener hear a loud burst of sound (beat maximum)?
questions.answer:
$f_{\text{beat}} = |f_1 - f_2| = |1000 - 1003| = 3\ \mathrm{Hz}$

The listener hears **3 loud bursts per second**.

Each loud burst corresponds to the two waves being momentarily in phase (maximum constructive interference).

questions.question: Two identical tuning forks vibrate at $f_0 = 500\ \mathrm{Hz}$. A small piece of wax is attached to one fork, reducing its frequency. 8 beats/s are observed. Find the new frequency of the wax-loaded fork.
questions.answer:
Adding wax increases mass, which decreases frequency.

$f_{\text{wax}} = f_0 - f_{\text{beat}} = 500 - 8 = 492\ \mathrm{Hz}$

(We know it's below 500 because wax lowers the frequency.)

$f_{\text{beat}} = |500 - 492| = 8\ \mathrm{Hz}$ ✓

questions.question: A listener walks between two loudspeakers emitting the same frequency. One speaker is stationary, the other moves away at $v_s = 2\ \mathrm{m/s}$. The listener (stationary) hears beats. Find the beat frequency if $f_0 = 680\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and $v = 340\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
questions.answer:
Stationary speaker frequency heard: $f_1 = 680\ \mathrm{Hz}$

Moving speaker (receding at $v_s = 2\ \mathrm{m/s}$) frequency heard:

$f_2 = f_0 \cdot \dfrac{v}{v + v_s} = 680 \times \dfrac{340}{342} \approx 680 \times 0.9942 \approx 676\ \mathrm{Hz}$

$f_{\text{beat}} = f_1 - f_2 = 680 - 676 = 4\ \mathrm{Hz}$
